## Conjugation

When you meet it: now L7 (singular) · past ήμουν L22 · future L17

| Person | Now | Past | Will |
|---|---|---|---|
| εγώ (I) | **είμαι** | **ήμουν** | **θα είμαι** |
| εσύ (you) | **είσαι** | **ήσουν** | **θα είσαι** |
| αυτός/ή/ό (he/she/it) | **είναι** | **ήταν** | **θα είναι** |
| εμείς (we) | **είμαστε** | **ήμασταν** | **θα είμαστε** |
| εσείς (you all) | **είστε** | **ήσασταν** | **θα είστε** |
| αυτοί/ές/ά (they) | **είναι** | **ήταν** | **θα είναι** |

## This week's story

> 1. Γύρισα... Μάλλον είναι η τελευταία μου επίσκεψη. — Τότε ας την κάνουμε ωραία. Μια τελετή στο δέντρο σου, θεία. (I'm back... It's probably my last visit. — Then let's make it beautiful. A ceremony at your tree, auntie.)
> 2. Θεία, φέτος μαζέψαμε χίλια κιλά! Ένα ποσό σαν χρυσάφι! — Όπως τότε! Νικάμε, παιδί μου! (Auntie, this year we harvested a thousand kilos! An amount like gold! — Just like back then! We're winning, my child!)

**Week of** Dec 7 to Dec 13 · **Class:** [[L06 Coffee plans at the kafeneio-student|L06 Coffee plans at the kafeneio]] ([[L06 Coffee plans at the kafeneio-student|student page]]) · **Running total:** 210 of 1,500

## This week's story

One line a day, same people, one scene. Read it from the top each day, then add today's line. On Sunday, read the whole thing aloud.

> [!quote]- The week in six lines
> 1. Τι θα πάρετε, κύριε; — Δύο καφέδες, παρακαλώ. Και οι δύο για μένα! — Δύο; Εγώ ποτέ δεν πίνω τόσο καφέ! (What will you have, sir? — Two coffees, please. Both for me! — Two? I never drink that much coffee!)
> 2. Λοιπόν; Πας στο χωριό; — Ναι, πριν τα Χριστούγεννα. — Τότε θα δεις το σπίτι... και τι έχει μέσα! (So? Are you going to the village? — Yes, before Christmas. — Then you'll see the house... and what's inside!)
> 3. Ίσως έρθω κι εγώ, λίγο μετά. — Αλήθεια; Ποιος είναι ο λόγος; — Η γιαγιά η δική μου μένει δύο χωριά πιο πέρα! (Maybe I'll come too, a little later. — Really? What's the reason? — My own grandma lives two villages further on!)
> 4. Ποιο χωριό; Μίλα αργά! — Κα-στρά-κι. Πολύ κοντά στο δικό σου! — Τέλεια! Τώρα είμαι έτοιμη! (Which village? Speak slowly! — Kas-tra-ki. Very close to yours! — Perfect! Now I'm ready!)
> 5. Είσαι σίγουρος ότι θα έρθεις; — Σίγουρος! Αγαπάω το χωριό μου. Είναι πολύ ωραίο. — Έχεις δίκιο. Το βλέπω στα μάτια σου! (Are you sure you'll come? — Sure! I love my village. It's really beautiful. — You're right. I can see it in your eyes!)
> 6. Θυμάμαι μια ιστορία από τη γιαγιά μου: κάποιος ψάχνει κάτι στο σπίτι σας. — Τι εννοείς; Ποιος; — Δεν ξέρω. Αλλά με νοιάζει. Μην αφήνεις το κλειδί πουθενά! (I remember a story from my grandma: someone is looking for something in your house. — What do you mean? Who? — I don't know. But I care. Don't leave the key anywhere!)

## This week's story

One line a day, same people, one scene. Read it from the top each day, then add today's line. On Sunday, read the whole thing aloud.

> [!quote]- The week in six lines
> 1. Μια φωτογραφία! Ο παππούς, η γιαγιά... και ποιο είναι το κορίτσι; — Η αδερφή μου, η Ελένη. Γλυκό κορίτσι. (A photo! Grandpa, grandma... and who's the girl? — My sister, Eleni. A sweet girl.)
> 2. Κι αυτός ο τύπος με το μουστάκι; — Εγώ! — Θεέ μου, παππού! Ήσουν πολύ ωραίος! — Ήμουν; Οπότε τώρα δεν είμαι; (And this guy with the mustache? — Me! — My God, grandpa! You were so handsome! — I was? So now I'm not?)
> 3. Και η Ελένη πού είναι τώρα; — Έφυγε γρήγορα για την Αμερική. Ήρθε πάλι μόνο μία φορά. — Ζει ακόμη; — Ναι! Και όλο γράφει γράμματα. (And where is Eleni now? — She left for America in a hurry. She came back only once. — Is she still alive? — Yes! And she's always writing letters.)

**Week of** Nov 9 to Nov 15 · **Class:** [[L03 Making plans-student|L03 Making plans]] ([[L03 Making plans-student|student page]]) · **Running total:** 90 of 1,500

## This week's story

One line a day, same people, one scene. Read it from the top each day, then add today's line. On Sunday, read the whole thing aloud.

> [!quote]- The week in six lines
> 1. Γιατί ένα κλειδί από την Ελλάδα; — Δεν ξέρω. Σήμερα εμείς ρωτάμε τη γιαγιά! — Καλά! Τι ώρα; (Why a key from Greece? — I don't know. Today we ask grandma! — Fine! What time?)
> 2. Τώρα στην Ελλάδα είναι βράδυ. — Τότε αύριο το πρωί, πριν το μάθημα; — Τέλεια! (Right now it's evening in Greece. — Then tomorrow morning, before class? — Perfect!)

## This week's story

One line a day, same people, one scene. Read it from the top each day, then add today's line. On Sunday, read the whole thing aloud.

> [!quote]- The week in six lines
> 1. Το σπίτι μου! Το κτίριο είναι ίδιο. — Το καταφέραμε! Είστε εδώ! (My house! The building is the same. — We made it! You're here!)

## This week's story

One line a day, same people, one scene. Read it from the top each day, then add today's line. On Sunday, read the whole thing aloud.

> [!quote]- The week in six lines
> 1. Καλημέρα! Ήρθε κάτι άλλο από τη γιαγιά. — Μια κάρτα! Η εκκλησία του χωριού. Γράφει κάτι; — Τίποτα. Τώρα κοίτα την άλλη πλευρά. (Good morning! Something else came from grandma. — A card! The village church. Does it say anything? — Nothing. Now look at the other side.)
> 2. Κοίτα: ο ήλιος, η θάλασσα, μια βάρκα... — Το χωριό είναι στη θάλασσα ή στο βουνό; — Και τα δύο! Είναι στο βουνό, πάνω από τη θάλασσα. (Look: the sun, the sea, a boat... — Is the village by the sea or on the mountain? — Both! It's on the mountain, above the sea.)
> 3. Ποιος είναι ο μικρός άνθρωπος στη βάρκα; — Ο μπαμπάς σου, όταν ήταν παιδί! — Σωστά! Έχει τα ίδια μάτια. Και είναι τόσο μικρός! (Who is the little person in the boat? — Your dad, when he was a kid! — Right! He has the same eyes. And he's so little!)
> 4. Και ο άντρας με το κλειδί στο χέρι; — Ο παππούς, φυσικά. — Δίνει το κλειδί στον μπαμπά; Γιατί; — Δεν ξέρω. Για τον παππού, εκείνο το σπίτι ήταν όλος ο κόσμος. (And the man with the key in his hand? — Grandpa, of course. — He's giving the key to dad? Why? — I don't know. For grandpa, that house was the whole world.)
> 5. Εδώ χιονίζει... Στο χωριό τι καιρό κάνει; — Τώρα βρέχει λίγο. Αλλά είναι πραγματικά ωραία, κορίτσι μου. (Here it's snowing... What's the weather like in the village? — Right now it's raining a little. But it's really lovely, my girl.)

# Fluent in a Year · week 47: Childhood

**Week of** Sep 13 to Sep 19 · **No class this week** · **Running total:** 1350 of 1,500

## This week's story

One line a day, same people, one scene. Read it from the top each day, then add today's line. On Sunday, read the whole thing aloud.

> [!quote]- The week in six lines
> 1. Εδώ ήταν το σχολείο μου... Τόσα χρόνια, και θυμάμαι τα πάντα. — Μαμά, δεν είσαι επισκέπτης εδώ. Κανονικά θα έπρεπε να μείνεις! (My school was here... So many years, and I remember everything. — Mom, you're not a visitor here. Really, you should stay!)
> 2. Μαρία! Καλά νέα! Το εργοστάσιο ανοίγει ξανά! — Βλέπεις; Ο ιερέας φέρνει πάντα καλά νέα! (Maria! Good news! The factory is opening again! — See? The priest always brings good news!)
> 3. Τι ιστορικό χωριό. Κάθε πέτρα έχει μια ιστορία. — Και κάθε έξοδος μαζί σου, μαμά! (What a historic village. Every stone has a story. — And so does every outing with you, mom!)

## This week's story

> 2. Κάνει ζεστό εδώ! Δεν φοβάσαι μόνη; — Όχι. Εμπιστεύομαι αυτό το σπίτι, μαμά. (It's warm here! Aren't you scared alone? — No. I trust this house, mom.)

> 6. Η γεύση του λαδιού... σαν όταν ήμουν παιδί! — Και μια ευχή: να είμαστε πάντα μαζί. (The taste of the oil... like when I was a child! — And a wish: that we'll always be together.)

# Fluent in a Year · week 6: Lost and found

**Week of** Nov 30 to Dec 6 · **Class:** [[L05 Lost items and the shop-student|L05 Lost items and the shop]] ([[L05 Lost items and the shop-student|student page]]) · **Running total:** 180 of 1,500

## This week's story

One line a day, same people, one scene. Read it from the top each day, then add today's line. On Sunday, read the whole thing aloud.

> [!quote]- The week in six lines
> 1. Πού είναι το κλειδί; Δεν το βρίσκω! — Ένα λεπτό... Ψάχνω. — Δύο λεπτά, πέντε λεπτά... μισή ώρα! Τίποτα! (Where is the key? I can't find it! — One minute... I'm looking. — Two minutes, five minutes... half an hour! Nothing!)
> 2. Νομίζω πως κάποιος το πήρε. — Ποιος; Είναι κάτι μικρό, έτσι. Δεν αξίζει ούτε ένα ευρώ! — Πάμε στο γραφείο, κάτω. (I think someone took it. — Who? It's something small, like this. It's not even worth one euro! — Let's go to the office downstairs.)
> 3. Ναι; Τι θέλετε εσείς; — Χάσαμε ένα κλειδί. Μόνο ένα, παλιό. — Ελάτε μαζί μου. (Yes? What can I do for you? — We lost a key. Just one, an old one. — Come with me.)
> 4. Εκεί, στο κουτί. Είναι σαν το δικό σας; — Όχι... Ακόμα τίποτα. Αρχίζω να φοβάμαι. (There, in the box. Is it like yours? — No... Still nothing. I'm starting to get scared.)
> 5. Εγώ μένω εδώ και ψάχνω. Εσύ πήγαινε σπίτι. — Ευχαριστώ, Νίκο. Ελπίζω να το βρεις. — Αν το βρω, το φέρνω αμέσως! (I'll stay here and keep looking. You go home. — Thanks, Niko. I hope you find it. — If I find it, I'll bring it right away!)
> 6. Μαμά, έχασα το κλειδί της γιαγιάς! — Δεν πειράζει. Γύρνα... Τι έχεις στο παλτό; — Το κλειδί! Στην τσέπη μου! Χαίρομαι τόσο! Τώρα φτάνω στο χωριό με το κλειδί! (Mom, I lost grandma's key! — It doesn't matter. Turn around... What's in your coat? — The key! In my pocket! I'm so glad! Now I'll get to the village with the key!)

> [!quote]- The week in six lines
> 1. Όταν ήμουν μικρή, η γη ήταν η ψυχή μας. — Γιαγιά, είσαι κουρασμένη; Κάτσε ήσυχη. — Όχι, κορίτσι μου. Θέλω να σου πω. (When I was little, the land was our soul. — Grandma, are you tired? Sit and rest. — No, my girl. I want to tell you.)
> 2. Η Ελένη ήταν σπουδαία. Ήξερε για κάθε σπόρο. — Θέλω να συζητήσουμε γι' αυτήν, γιαγιά. Για όλα. (Eleni was remarkable. She knew about every seed. — I want us to talk about her, grandma. About everything.)

> 4. Εξήγησέ μου: γιατί έφυγε η Ελένη; — Ο άντρας της ήταν άρρωστος. (Explain to me: why did Eleni leave? — Her husband was sick.)
> 5. Ο σύζυγός της χρειαζόταν γιατρό στην Αμερική. Έκλεισαν το σπίτι και έφυγαν. — Κι εσύ μάζευες τις ελιές της; — Κάθε χρόνο. (Her husband needed a doctor in America. They closed up the house and left. — And you harvested her olives? — Every year.)
> 6. Φύτεψα ένα δέντρο για την Ελένη, στην άκρη του χωραφιού. — Ένα δέντρο; Γιατί; — Ψάξε εκεί, και θα καταλάβεις. (I planted a tree for Eleni, at the edge of the field. — A tree? Why? — Look there, and you'll understand.)

## This week's story

One line a day, same people, one scene. Read it from the top each day, then add today's line. On Sunday, read the whole thing aloud.

> [!quote]- The week in six lines
> 1. Η βασιλόπιτα! Ένα κομμάτι για το σπίτι, ένα για τον Χριστό... — Πόσα κομμάτια; Δέκα; — Όχι, έξι! Τρία για εμάς, τρία για τους άλλους. (The vasilopita! A piece for the house, one for Christ... — How many pieces? Ten? — No, six! Three for us, three for the others.)
> 2. Γιαγιά, ποιο κομμάτι είναι για μένα; — Το τέσσερα. Καλή χρονιά, κορίτσι μου! — Μα κι εγώ; Δεν έχω κομμάτι! — Έχεις, Νίκο: το πέντε! (Grandma, which piece is for me? — Number four. Happy New Year, my girl! — But what about me? I don't have a piece! — You do, Niko: number five!)
> 3. Εγώ πρώτος! ... Τίποτα. Το κομμάτι μου είναι χωρίς φλουρί. — Όμως υπομονή, Νίκο. Κάθε κομμάτι έχει την τύχη του. (Me first! ... Nothing. My piece has no coin. — But be patient, Niko. Every piece has its own luck.)
> 4. Μόλις δάγκωσα κάτι σκληρό! — Το φλουρί! Ακριβώς στο δικό σου κομμάτι! (I just bit into something hard! — The coin! Right in your piece!)
> 5. Χίλια μπράβο, Μαρία! Καλή τύχη για όλη τη χρονιά. — Και τώρα, με το κλειδί, πάμε στην παλιά πόρτα; — Τώρα; Είναι έντεκα το βράδυ! — Ε, και; Πάμε! (A thousand bravos, Maria! Good luck for the whole year. — And now, with the key, shall we go to the old door? — Now? It's eleven at night! — So what? Let's go!)
> 6. Είναι νύχτα... Και μπροστά μας, το παλιό σπίτι. — Η καρδιά μου χτυπάει δυνατά! — Κι η δική μου. Άνοιξε! (It's night... And in front of us, the old house. — My heart is pounding! — Mine too. Open it!)

## This week's story

> [!quote]- The week in six lines
> 1. Καλησπέρα! Πόσα άτομα; — Δύο, παρακαλώ. Τι έχετε σήμερα; — Φρέσκο ψάρι! Και κρύα μπίρα. (Good evening! How many people? — Two, please. What do you have today? — Fresh fish! And cold beer.)
> 2. Ένα ψάρι για μένα. Κι εσύ; Κρέας; — Όχι, εγώ δεν τρώω κρέας. Ένα ποτήρι κρασί και μια σαλάτα. (A fish for me. And you? Meat? — No, I don't eat meat. A glass of wine and a salad.)

> 5. Η Ελένη ήταν δυνατή γυναίκα. Έκρυψε τα τετράδιά της σε τουλάχιστον επτά μέρη. — Σοβαρά; Επτά; (Eleni was a strong woman. She hid her notebooks in at least seven places. — Seriously? Seven?)
> 6. Ένα ποτό από μένα, με μέλι. — Ευχαριστώ! ... Τι περίεργο... Στο ποτήρι, ένα μικρό κλειδί! — Ήταν της Ελένης. Τώρα είναι δικό σου. (A drink on me, with honey. — Thank you! ... How strange... In the glass, a little key! — It was Eleni's. Now it's yours.)

**Week of** Oct 18 to Oct 24 · **No class this week** · **Running total:** 1500 of 1,500

## This week's story

One line a day, same people, one scene. Read it from the top each day, then add today's line. On Sunday, read the whole thing aloud.

> [!quote]- The week in six lines
> 1. Νίκο, έχω ιδέα! Ένα κατάστημα στο παλιό γκαράζ! — Είναι ρίσκο... αλλά και υπόσχεση! Ας το κάνουμε! (Niko, I have an idea! A shop in the old garage! — It's a risk... but also a promise! Let's do it!)
> 2. Μαμά, το αποφάσισα: μετακομίζω στο χωριό. — Το ήξερα! Ακούω το χαμόγελό σου από εδώ! (Mom, I've decided: I'm moving to the village. — I knew it! I can hear your smile from here!)
> 3. Τι σύμπτωση! Σήμερα ήρθαν όλα τα χαρτιά. — Τέλεια! Χωρίς άγχος, επιτέλους! (What a coincidence! All the papers came today. — Perfect! No more stress, at last!)
> 4. Αφήνεις μια καλή δουλειά στην Αμερική. Σέβομαι την απόφασή σου. — Ευχαριστώ. Είμαι ευγνώμων για όλα. (You're leaving a good job in America. I respect your decision. — Thank you. I'm grateful for everything.)
> 5. Υπογράψτε εδώ... Είναι νόμιμο! Το σπίτι, το χωράφι, όλα δικά σας. — Ο προπονητής μου στο σχολείο θα φώναζε: γκολ! (Sign here... It's legal! The house, the field, all yours. — My coach at school would shout: goal!)
> 6. Μαρία, σου έχω μια δουλειά στην Αθήνα, με καλό μισθό! — Ευχαριστώ, αλλά όχι για μένα. Εγώ έχω μια φάρμα. Θα τα πούμε! (Maria, I have a job for you in Athens, with a good salary! — Thank you, but not for me. I have a farm. See you!)

> 1. Απόψε στο θέατρο: συζήτηση για το μέλλον του χωριού. — Έχω μια βασική ερώτηση: θα μείνουν οι νέοι; — Αν έχουν δουλειά, ναι. Όπως εσύ! (Tonight at the theater: a discussion about the village's future. — I have a basic question: will young people stay? — If they have work, yes. Like you!)

> 5. Σάντουιτς για όλους! — Γιαγιά, στις δύο το πρωί; Έλα εδώ, μια αγκαλιά! (Sandwiches for everyone! — Grandma, at two in the morning? Come here, a hug!)

> 2. Πάμε, παππού. Πρώτα στην τράπεζα, μετά στο φαρμακείο. — Πονάει το δόντι; Δοκιμάστε αυτό, παππού. — Ευχαριστώ, κορίτσι μου. (Let's go, grandpa. First to the bank, then to the pharmacy. — Does the tooth hurt? Try this, grandpa. — Thank you, my girl.)
> 3. Έχω κι ένα άλλο πρόβλημα: το σπίτι είναι της Ελένης, όχι δικό μας. — Η κόρη μου είναι δικηγόρος. Μην το ξεχάσετε! — Αντί για φάρμακο, μια δικηγόρος! (I have another problem too: the house is Eleni's, not ours. — My daughter is a lawyer. Don't forget that! — Instead of medicine, a lawyer!)

# Fluent in a Year · week 43: Sport

**Week of** Aug 16 to Aug 22 · **No class this week** · **Running total:** 1230 of 1,500

## This week's story

One line a day, same people, one scene. Read it from the top each day, then add today's line. On Sunday, read the whole thing aloud.

> [!quote]- The week in six lines

# Greekquent Groups

**Real Greek, real people, real conversation.** Θα τα πούμε.

You have learned the words. Now use them. Greekquent Groups are small live conversations where you talk with other Greekquent students. Your teacher guides the conversation and keeps it moving, but you and the other students do most of the talking.

> [!tip]- Why join
> - **More speaking time.** In a lesson you answer your teacher. In a group you have to keep a conversation going, the way you will in Greece.
> - **Real situations.** Each session builds on the scenario you are studying: ordering at a taverna, visiting a Greek home, asking for directions, shopping and making plans.
> - **Just hard enough.** The topics are set so you get most of it right, and the parts you miss show you what to work on next.
> - **People to practice with.** You will meet other learners at your level, and you can keep practicing with them between sessions.
> - **Extra practice.** Groups don't replace your regular lessons. They give you more practice on top of them.

> [!info]- How to unlock it
> You can join once you reach one of these:
> - you have finished all 26 lessons of Year One
> - you have reached a Fluent in a Year milestone (750 words)
> - your teacher invites you
>
> Not there yet? Keep going. Every lesson and every set of 5 words gets you closer.

> [!example]- What a session looks like
> - **Size:** 4 to 6 students, so everyone gets to talk.
> - **Length:** about an hour.
> - **Format:**
>   - a quick warm-up
>   - a scenario or discussion prompt
>   - conversation in pairs and as a whole group
>   - a short wrap-up with useful phrases to take home
> - **Bring:** your textbook and planner, plus any words you marked red or yellow this week.

> [!summary]- Price
> | Option | Price |
> |---|---|
> | Drop in | $12 per session |
> | Subscription | $10 per session |
>
> - **Introductory rate:** these prices are for early members and may go up later. Join now to lock in the lower rate.
> - **Join as often as you like:** you can come to more than one group a week.

> [!question]- How to join
> Ask your teacher at your next lesson. If you have unlocked Groups, you will get the schedule and a sign-up link.
>
> Teach Greek yourself? Ask about teaching with Greekquent.

# 05 Listening and News

Two ways the course reaches outside the classroom: the Teach Yourself audio for listening at home, and a short "news minute" that connects Greek to what is happening this week.

> [!note]- Teach Yourself audio: how to assign it
> The class book is **Beginners' Greek** by Aristarhos Matsukas (Teach Yourself, 2025, ISBN 9781399821438), previously published as Get Started in Greek ([book page](https://us.teachyourself.com/products/beginners-greek)). The audio is free in the **Teach Yourself Library** app ([iPhone/iPad](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/teach-yourself-library/id1143087176) · [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=net.trellisys.papertrell.shelf9ec79a53123947bea89b912e71161bfd)) or streamed on the [Teach Yourself audio page](https://library.teachyourself.com/id007706138/Beginners-Greek-Audio). Files can't be saved to a computer, and there are no links to individual tracks, so every lesson gives one stable link plus a line of text naming the exact track numbers to choose (for example 03.04 Conversation 1).
>
> 1. Students install the app once, in week 1, and add the free Beginners' Greek audio.
> 2. Each lesson note has an **Assign audio** line, and the student page and textbook repeat it.
> 3. Routine: listen once without the book, once with the book, once saying it along (shadowing). About 10 minutes.
> 4. Don't copy or re-upload the audio. Point students to the app.
>
> Track numbers match the web player list: 0.01–0.07 alphabet and pronunciation, then Units 1–10. Units are matched to lessons by topic from the book's contents page (for example Unit 10 Στη λαϊκή αγορά with Lesson 12 Laiki, Unit 8 daily routine with Lessons 10 and 14). Most units are split over two lessons: Vocab Builder to Conversation 1, then the rest. Lessons without a matching unit replay earlier conversations and retell them. > [!tip]- News minute: Greek in the news (5 minutes, optional)
> Once a week, at the start of the warm-up:

# 09 Games

Links: [[Today]] · [[00 Greekquent Index]] · [[07 Fluent in a Year]]

All four games are part of the vault. They open here in Obsidian, need no internet, and update with the vault.

> [!summary]- Greekquent Buzzer (fastest fingers)
> [Open the Greekquent Buzzer](obsidian://greekquent?open=buzzer) (works offline)
> - Lay the phone flat between two students sitting face to face. The screen is split, so each student reads their own half the right way up.
> - Each round shows an English word and two Greek choices. First correct tap wins the point. A wrong tap locks that student out, so the other can still answer.
> - **Words from:** a lesson (phrases and words), a Fluent in a Year week, or the top 50 to 1,500 words. You can mix in earlier lessons or weeks.
> - **Options:** play to 5, 10, or 15. Reverse mode (Greek prompt, English choices). The phone says the Greek answer aloud. 7-second rounds.
> - Missed words come back a few rounds later. At the end, the app lists them so students can mark them red on their printed list.
> - The end screen shows each player's hit rate. Aim for about 85% right over a few games.
> - Free, with no accounts. On Today, open **More** and tap **Play Buzzer with these** to play today's or review words. Turn off auto-lock and silent mode before class.

> [!summary]- Greekquent Cousins (spot the English cousin)
> [Open Greekquent Cousins](obsidian://greekquent?open=cousins) (works offline)
> - The same face-to-face split screen as the Buzzer, plus **Solo practice** for remote students. Works on iPhone and Android.
> - **Find the cousin:** a Greek word and two English words. Pick the cousin (χρόνος: chronology or chocolate).
> - **Guess the meaning:** a Greek word and its cousin. Pick what the Greek word means (φόβος, cousin phobia: fear or star).
> - **Levels:** Twins (ιδέα, idea), Cousins (καρδιά, cardiac), Hidden cousins (σπίτι, hospital; γεια, hygiene). 157 pairs, all from the 1,500.
> - **Letter rules:** the setup screen lists them (χ → ch, φ → ph, θ → th, ψ → ps, ξ → x, υ → y, κ → c, initial vowel → h), and you can play only the words for one rule. Every answer shows the rule and a one-line bridge, for example "Strategy was first the art of leading an army."
> - 85% hit-rate check and a missed list at the end, like the Buzzer.

> [!summary]- Greekquent Γιαγιά (find the notebooks, don't get fed)
> [Open Greekquent Γιαγιά](obsidian://greekquent?open=giagia) (works offline)
> - One player, made for kids and remote students. Works on iPhone and Android (d-pad or swipe) and with arrow keys on a computer.
> - Walk around the house (Κουζίνα, Σαλόνι, Διάδρομος, Υπνοδωμάτιο, Μπάνιο, Μπαλκόνι) and find 7 τετράδια. Each one says a Greek word aloud and gives three English meanings.
> - Right answer: Γιαγιά stops for 2 seconds ("Μπράβο!"). Wrong answer: she gets a little faster, and the notebook stays so the word comes back.
> - She catches you 3 times and it's dinner ("Φάε, παιδί μου!"). Find all 7 and the door opens.
> - **Words from:** any kid lesson (with earlier lessons mixed in), the top 100, 300 or all 1,500, or today's words from the Today page.
> - The end screen lists missed words with Hear buttons and can send them to Review on Today.

> [!summary]- Greekquent Story Lines (watch it, then play it)
> [Open Story Lines](obsidian://greekquent?open=story) (works offline)
> - **The whole year:** 300 days, one story. Μαρία, Νίκος and the family follow the notebooks of a great-aunt to a house in the village. Pick any week and day.
> - **Watch:** each day's story line as a short cartoon. The Greek subtitles light up word by word as the characters speak, and things appear when their word is said. Slower and English buttons; Whole week plays Monday to Saturday.
> - **Text adventure:** the same scene as an 80s-style text game. It only moves on when you type the right Greek word. Greeklish works too (nero = νερό), so no Greek keyboard is needed. HELP gives a clue; after two misses, three word buttons appear.
> - Works on iPhone and Android.
> - On Today, tap **Watch it** or **Play it as a text adventure** under the day's line.

> [!summary]- Run it in class
> 1. Pick the current lesson, play to 5.
> 2. Winner stays, the next student challenges.
> 3. Last round of the night: the Fluent in a Year week with earlier weeks mixed in.

# Classroom Greek

The same phrases every class, all year. Learn your side once and you can stay in Greek even when you're lost. Do the gesture every time you say it. Back to [[Today]].

> [!tip]- Why this works
> Set phrases you hear every week stick without studying, because they come up so often and you need them. They also buy you time to think. Saying "Ένα λεπτό…" beats switching to English.

## Your side: staying in Greek

```greekquent-say
Πώς λέμε «…» στα ελληνικά; | How do you say "…" in Greek? | Point at your mouth, then shrug.
Τι σημαίνει «…»; | What does "…" mean? | Tap your temple, eyebrows up.
Δεν κατάλαβα. | I didn't understand. | Shake your head slowly, hand flat by your ear.
Ξανά, παρακαλώ. | Again, please. | Roll your hand forward in a circle.
Πιο αργά, παρακαλώ. | Slower, please. | Push both palms down slowly.
Ένα λεπτό… | One moment… | Hold up one finger.
Δεν ξέρω. | I don't know. | Shrug with palms up.
Νομίζω… | I think… | Tap your temple.
Έτσι; | Like this? | Palms out, as if offering it.
Σωστά; | Right? | Thumb half up, eyebrows up.
Συγγνώμη. | Sorry. | Hand on your chest.
Μπορώ να το πω στα αγγλικά; | Can I say it in English? | Make a small "E" with your fingers. Use it only when you really need to.
```

## The teacher's side: what you will hear

```greekquent-say
Γεια σας! Ξεκινάμε. | Hello, everyone. Let's begin. | Big wave, then clap once.
Ακούστε. | Listen. | Cup your hand behind your ear.
Επαναλάβετε. | Repeat. | Point to your mouth, then to the class.
Όλοι μαζί. | All together. | Sweep both arms in.
Ξανά. | Again. | Roll your hand forward in a circle.
Πιο δυνατά. | Louder. | Palms up, lift them.
Σειρά σου. | Your turn. | Open hand toward one person.
Ποιος θέλει; | Who wants to? | Hand up high, looking around.
Σε ζευγάρια. | In pairs. | Two fingers, then point at a partner.
Γυρίστε τα χαρτιά. | Turn your papers over. | Flip your hand over.
Μπράβο! Σωστά! | Well done. That's right. | Thumbs up.
Σχεδόν. | Almost. | Flat hand, tilt it side to side.
Καταλάβατε; | Did you understand? | Answer with a thumb: up, sideways or down.
Στα αγγλικά: | In English (a short English moment). | Fingers make an "E". It ends when the teacher says "Πάμε πάλι στα ελληνικά."
Τελειώσαμε. Θα τα πούμε! | We're done. See you. | Wave.
```

## Thumbs mean colors

When the teacher asks **Καταλάβατε;**, answer with your thumb. **Up** is green (got it), **sideways** is yellow (kind of), **down** is red (not yet). These are the same three colors as your word list.

## The weekly rally

Every class starts with a quick back-and-forth in Greek, the same shape each week: the teacher asks, you answer, then you swap and ask. The lines are on each lesson page under **Rally**. Practice your side before class: on Today, tap **Practice my side**.

# Setting up

Two minutes, once. Back to [[Today]].

> [!tip]- 1. Turn on the Greekquent tools
> The first time you open the vault, Obsidian asks whether you trust it. Tap **Trust author and enable plugins**. If you missed it: Settings, Community plugins, **Turn on community plugins**.

> [!tip]- 2. The four tool buttons (Today, Look up, Ask, More)
> These are small icons, not the colored buttons on word notes. On a computer they sit in the thin strip of icons along the far left edge of the window. On a phone, tap the menu button (three lines) at the bottom right of the screen, when you are not typing in a note.
> - **Today** (house): the Story puzzle, one sentence at a time from part 1 at your own pace (read the English, then build it in Greek from word tiles; touch a tile to hear it), comebacks, this week's class, and words to review. Doing Fluent in a Year? Tap **Show its words** at the bottom once and its five words appear, one at a time. Kids use their own vault, **Greekquent Kids**.
> - **Look up** (magnifying glass): any word in English or Greek. Words outside the 1,500 are translated right in the box. Tick Guess first to try before you see the answer.
> - **Ask** (two people): a question about the note you are on, ready to share in the class GroupMe. You can also ask on video from there.
> - **More** (three dots): More on this page, Word web, Send homework, Share feedback, What's new, Update vault.

> [!tip]- Less on the page, more in the side panel
> Lessons and word notes show the main things first. The extras (word pairs, words that go together, review prompts, word links) sit in the side panel: tap **More on this page** near the top of a lesson or on a word's button row. On a phone it slides in from the right. Every other article lives in the **Extras** folder.

> [!tip]- 3. Color your words
> Every word note has a row of buttons just under the meaning, lined up with the text: **Hear it**, **More**, and three colors: **Don't have it** (red), **Kind of** (yellow), **Have it** (green). Tap one after you try to say the word from memory. Tap it again to clear it. Red words come back on the Today page.

> [!tip]- 4. Your own notes
> Type in the **My Work** folder: Homework, My Notes, and anything you add. Updates never change My Work. Other notes open read-only so they can't change by accident.

> [!tip]- 5. Weekly updates
> When Obsidian says an update is ready, tap the message. Or tap More, then Update vault. Only changed files download.

# 02 Verb Tables

Back to [[00 Greekquent Index]] · lessons in [[01 Lesson Scripts]]

Printable version: ![[Greekquent Verb Sheet Year One.pdf]]

Twelve core verbs, each conjugated in full on its own word note. "When you meet it" gives the lesson where each form first shows up in Year One.

## How Greek time works

- **Now:** one present tense. Endings for most verbs: -ω, -εις, -ει, -ουμε, -ετε, -ουν. Stressed -ώ verbs like μπορώ: -ώ, -είς, -εί, -ούμε, -είτε, -ούν.
- **Two pasts:** "was doing / used to" (έβλεπα) and "did once" (είδα). Some verbs (έχω, θέλω, είμαι, κάνω, ξέρω) use one form for both.
- **Past endings:** -α, -ες, -ε, -αμε, -ατε, -αν. The stress moves back to the third syllable from the end. When the word is too short for that, an έ- is added in front (βλέπω → έβλεπα, but βλέπαμε).
- **Future:** θα + verb. θα + the "once" form is the everyday "will" (θα δω, I'll see). θα + the present form means "will be doing" or "will regularly" (θα βλέπω).
- **The same "once" form follows να:** Θέλω να δω. Μπορώ να φάω; That's why these show up as chunks long before the future is taught.

## The anchor verbs

- [[έχω]] — I have · έχω, είχα, θα έχω
- [[θέλω]] — I want · θέλω, ήθελα, θα θέλω
- [[μπορώ]] — I can · μπορώ, μπορούσα, μπόρεσα, θα μπορέσω
- [[βλέπω]] — I see · βλέπω, έβλεπα, είδα, θα δω

## Everyday verbs

- [[είμαι]] — I am · είμαι, ήμουν, θα είμαι
- [[κάνω]] — I do, I make · κάνω, έκανα, θα κάνω
- [[πάω]] — I go · πάω, πήγαινα, πήγα, θα πάω
- [[τρώω]] — I eat · τρώω, έτρωγα, έφαγα, θα φάω
- [[πίνω]] — I drink · πίνω, έπινα, ήπια, θα πιω
- [[ξέρω]] — I know · ξέρω, ήξερα, θα ξέρω
- [[λέω]] — I say · λέω, έλεγα, είπα, θα πω
- [[μιλάω]] — I speak, I talk · μιλάω, μιλούσα, μίλησα, θα μιλήσω

## Ledger: when each form arrives

| Form | έχω | θέλω | μπορώ | βλέπω |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| I (1st singular) | L1 | L2 | L3 | L4 |
| you, he/she (singular) | L2 | L2 | L3 | L4 |
| negative with δεν | L3 oral / L5 read | L3 / L5 | L3 / L5 | L5 |
| polite / plural you (-ετε) | L12 | L4 chunk | L19 | L9 |
| full plural | L9 | L9 | L9 | L9 |
| + να + verb | — | L10 | L10 | να δω L5 |
| future θα | L17 | L17 | L17 | θα δω L17 |
| past | είχα L22 | ήθελα L22 | μπορούσα L22 | έβλεπα L22 / είδα L23 |

# 07 Fluent in a Year

An optional homework tier for students who want the whole 1,500-word list in one year: **5 words a day, 6 days a week, for 300 days**. Sunday is review. The class lessons alone cover about 250 list words; this tier covers the rest, so every word a student meets in class counts toward the 1,500.

To see each day's five words on [[Today]], tap **Show its words** at the bottom of Today once. Tap **Hide on Today** to turn it off.

> [!info]- How it works
> - **52 weeks**, starting the week of Lesson 1 (Oct 26) and running to the following October: 50 word weeks of 30 words, plus two rest weeks at Christmas.
> - **Order:** that week's lesson words come first. The rest are the next most frequent words on the list, chosen to fit the week's lesson scene or theme where they can. The learner essentials at the end of the list (days, colours, school things) are spread through the year instead of waiting for the last weeks.
> - **Real scenes, not rote lists:** every word has a real example sentence, every week ends with a scene task (a 4-line dialogue using 5 of the week's words), and the group meet prompt uses them out loud.
> - **Markers:** black-mark each word the day it starts; re-mark red, yellow, or green on Sunday.
> - **Anki:** import `Extras/Handouts/Greekquent Fluent in a Year Anki Deck.csv`. Cards are tagged `fiay::w01`… by week and `fiay::d001`… by day, so students can unsuspend one day at a time.
> - **After class ends (May):** weeks 30–52 keep going over the summer and into the fall with themed weeks (beach, ferry, hotel, work, news, olive harvest). The group meet carries the speaking.

> [!tip]- Group meet (once a week, about 30 minutes)
> 1. Warm-up: everyone reads their scene-task dialogue with a partner (5 min).
> 2. The two prompt questions, round the circle. Answer, then ask the next person (10 min).
> 3. The bridge task: one step past the lesson (10 min).
> 4. Each person names one word from the week they will use tomorrow (5 min).
> Lesson weeks tie the prompt to that lesson. Other weeks bridge to the next skill (past stories, future plans, opinions).

# 04 How Memory Works

Back to [[00 Greekquent Index]] · [[01 Lesson Scripts]]

The lesson notes stay short. This note explains why they're built the way they are. Each move below already sits inside every lesson, at the step where it happens.

| Move | Where it is in every lesson |
|---|---|
| Count recalls, not repetitions | Recall 1, 2, 3 in the lesson, then the review ring at 1, 2, 4, and 8 lessons back |
| Come back to it after a gap | Recall 2 comes after the main scene and fork rounds, not right after teaching |
| Say it, don't pick it | Review cards, recall points, and Anki: English cue, Greek answer out loud |
| Guess first | The first 30 seconds of the warm-up |
| Mix it up | A "Mix-in" line from the review cards in the fork rounds |
| Act it out | The gesture table, folded inside each warm-up |
| Same story, less time | The retell round, the last replay in Fork it |
| Write it by hand | Exit-ticket index cards, and the textbook's writing lines |
| Move the words | The tile round in Fork it |
| Keep the four strands balanced | The 60-minute flow, plus homework |

## Count recalls, not repetitions

There is no magic number of repetitions. A 2019 meta-analysis of 26 studies found a medium effect of repetition on vocabulary learning, and the effect depended on spacing, picture support, and how engaged learners were ([Uchihara, Webb & Yanagisawa, 2019](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/lang.12343)). The number of encounters needed ranged from about 2 to 20 ([summary of that meta-analysis](https://centaur.reading.ac.uk/108688/8/13621688221140521.pdf)).

A more useful target is successful recalls. Rawson and Dunlosky recommend recalling an item correctly 3 times when first learning it, then relearning it 3 more times at widely spaced intervals ([Rawson & Dunlosky, 2011](https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ934616)). This course gives each phrase 3 recalls in its own lesson and about 4 more in the review ring, so about 7 recalls over two months.

## Come back to it after a gap

Recalling something you've already got right still pays off. In one study, repeated recall of items students already knew improved retention by more than 100% compared with dropping them from practice, while re-reading them added nothing ([Karpicke & Roediger, 2007](https://learninglab.psych.purdue.edu/downloads/2007/2007_Karpicke_Roediger_JML.pdf)).

Gaps between sessions matter even more than gaps within one class. Students who recalled items once in each of three spaced sessions remembered more than twice as much as students who recalled them three times in one session ([Association for Psychological Science summary](https://www.psychologicalscience.org/observer/teaching-current-directions-studying-psychopathology)). That's why the review ring at the start of each class is the backbone, and the in-class recalls are the support.

## Say it, don't pick it

After a week, students who had been tested on a passage recalled 61% of it, against 40% for students who had re-read it four times ([Roediger & Karpicke, 2006](https://learninglab.psych.purdue.edu/downloads/2006/2006_Roediger_Karpicke_PsychSci.pdf)). Producing an answer helps more than recognizing it among choices ([review summary](https://notes.andymatuschak.org/zGfjkW1ociSmSUCLcpbhKjf)). So every check in this course is an English cue with a spoken Greek answer, papers face-down.

## Guess first

Asking learners to guess an answer before they're taught it improves later memory for that answer, even when the guess is wrong ([review of pretesting research](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10648-023-09814-5)). In class, take two or three guesses, praise any that are close, and then teach the phrase. Keep it to 30 seconds.

## Mix it up

Mixing different kinds of practice, instead of doing one kind at a time, has a moderate benefit on average ([meta-analysis, Brunmair & Richter, 2019](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31556629/)). In Fork it, one line from the day's review cards goes into a replay, so old and new phrases share the same scene.

## Act it out

Words learned with gestures were recalled better at every check, including after 14 months ([Macedonia, 2014](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4260465/)). Two things matter: the gesture has to match the meaning, and students have to make it themselves, because watching the teacher do it isn't enough ([same review](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4260465/)).

Greek caution: never push an open palm with spread fingers toward someone. That's the μούτζα, the most traditional Greek insult ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountza)). The OK ring made with thumb and forefinger is also obscene in Greece ([Cultural Atlas](https://theculturalatlas.org/greek-culture/greek-culture-communication)). The gestures in these notes wave with the fingers together, keep "open hand" gestures palm-up, and count with the palm facing yourself.

## Same story, less time

In Paul Nation's 4/3/2 activity, a learner tells the same story to three listeners in turn, in 4, then 3, then 2 minutes. Studies found gains in fluency, and also in grammatical accuracy and complexity ([Nation, 2007](https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/lals/resources/paul-nations-resources/paul-nations-publications/publications/documents/2007-Four-strands.pdf)). Nation suggests shorter times for beginners ([Nation](https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/lals/resources/paul-nations-resources/paul-nations-publications/publications/documents/foreign-language_1125.pdf)), so the retell round here uses 60/45/30 seconds in Lessons 1–8, 90/60/45 seconds in Lessons 9–16, and 2 minutes/90 seconds/1 minute from Lesson 17.

## Write it by hand

Handwriting helps most with learning a new alphabet. Adults learning Arabic letters by writing them by hand learned faster than those who typed them or watched videos, and they were better at reading and spelling new words ([Wiley & Rapp, 2021, Johns Hopkins summary](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2021/07/210708111508.htm)). That's why the textbook has letter-writing rows in Lessons 1–6.

For vocabulary in general, the evidence is mixed. An EEG study found more brain connectivity during handwriting than typing ([van der Weel & van der Meer, 2024](https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2023.1219945/full)), but critics point out that the study measured no actual learning ([commentary](https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2024.1517235/full)). So writing by hand here always comes paired with recall: students write from memory, not just copy.

## Move the words with your hands

Sentence tiles haven't been tested the way the moves above have, so treat them as a way to do recall and production with your hands. Building a sentence from an English cue is production, not recognition. Flipping, negating, and swapping tiles is the same slot-swap forking the class does out loud, done on the table. The tiles also make word order visible: the shaded verb tile anchors the sentence, and δεν always goes right before it.

## Keep the four strands balanced

Nation's four strands are input (listening and reading), output (speaking and writing), deliberate study, and fluency. He suggests about a quarter of the time for each, counting study outside class ([Nation, 1996](https://www.wgtn.ac.nz/lals/resources/paul-nations-resources/paul-nations-publications/publications/documents/1996-Four-strands.pdf)).

A rough tally for one class:

| Block | Min | Mostly |
|---|---|---|
| Spaced review | 10 | Fluency (known phrases, at speed) |
| Warm-up | 15 | Deliberate study (new phrases, boards, gestures) |
| Main scene | 15 | Input (first read-through) and output (performing) |
| Fork it | 12 | Output (replays) and fluency (retell round) |
| Exit ticket | 5 | Deliberate study |

That's roughly 20 minutes of study, 10 of input, 15 of output, and 15 of fluency. Input is the thin strand in class. Two cheap fixes: read the main scene aloud once while students just listen before they read it themselves, and lean on the homework (re-reading the story daily, the watch-list), which Nation counts toward input.

## At home

- **Anki:** say the answer out loud before flipping the card, and press Again until each card is right once that day. Anki then spaces the next review itself.
- **Paper packet:** the red, yellow, and green markers already work as a spaced schedule. Review red words every day, yellow every few days, green now and then.

> - New note: **[[11 Classroom Greek]]**, the same phrases every class, with a Hear button and a gesture for each. Learn your side once, and you can stay in Greek when you're stuck.
> - Class now opens with a short **rally** in Greek: the teacher asks, you answer, then you swap. Lesson 5 is the first one, under **Rally** on the lesson page.
> - On Today, **This week's rally** shows up the week before class. Tap **Practice my side** to hear each question, answer out loud, then check.

> [!info]- November 17, late: A big card, only when it helps
> - **Practice it** on today's line opens one big card in front of the page: listen, say it from memory, then check. Mark it said from there.
> - **Quiz me** on Comebacks shows one line at a time: English first, say it, then reveal the Greek.
> - Sunday: **Read it line by line** walks through the week's story one line per card, then all together.
> - Close it with ×, Esc, or a tap outside. Swipe or use the arrows to move. Everything else on Today stays a plain list.

> [!info]- November 17, night: Instructions that match the buttons
> - **Today is back to the list of cards**, top to bottom. The slides will return later, only for a few moments where one big card helps.
> - Word notes no longer tell you to tap a button your layout hides. "Pair it with" now says: take one word from each line and say it out loud.
> - Video questions: the steps now point to Ask, then Ask on video instead.
> - Kids have their own vault, **Greekquent Kids**: this week's game, one line a day, the swap, this week's words and the moves, with no grown-up tools. The Kid track here still works.

> [!info]- November 17, evening: One card at a time
> - **Today is now a set of slides.** One big card at a time: today's line, comebacks, today's words, review and the rest. Swipe left or right on a phone, or use the arrows. The dots show where you are.
> - Today remembers your card when it updates (after you mark a color or say a line), and starts again at the first card each morning.
> - The tool buttons (Look up a word, Send homework) stay underneath, always one tap away.

> [!info]- November 17, later: Genders that agree
> - **The graph follows the noun.** Tap a noun in the word graph and the describing words around it switch to its gender: tap η πόλη and μεγάλος becomes μεγάλη, ο becomes η, ένας becomes μία. Nouns now show their article, so you always see the gender.
> - **Agrees with strip.** Under the word's name you get ready phrases to tap and hear, like μεγάλη πόλη and αρχαία πόλη. Open a describing word like μεγάλος to see it change with each noun: μεγάλο σπίτι, μεγάλη πόλη, μεγάλος αδερφός.
> - **Story links in the graph.** Words that meet in this year's story now link to each other (see "Together in the story" on a word note). That makes many more sparks. A story spark shows the scene where the words met.
> - **Story Lines cards fixed.** A card now shows the form that was said, so το κινητό shows το, not ο. In the text adventure the wrong gender gets "Almost. Right word, but it has to agree with the noun."

> [!info]- November 17: The whole year as one story
> - **Story Lines for all 300 days.** Every day's line on Today is now part of one story that runs the whole year. Tap **Watch it** or **Play it** under the line. Both open right here in the vault, no browser or internet needed. Γιαγιά opens here too.
> - **Sparks in the word graph.** Some words keep turning up together, like ζωή, άνθρωπος and χάνω. When you open a word in the graph, Greekquent finds three that all link to each other and lights them up in gold. Tap **One sentence** to use all three in one sentence, then save it to My pairs. **Another** shows the next spark.
> - **Η and Ο read right.** The voice no longer reads a capital Η or Ο at the start of a sentence as a letter name.

> [!info]- November 16, night: One page at a time
> - **No more piles of tabs.** Links now open in the same page. Use Back and Forward to move through what you've opened. Any extra tabs from before close on their own (notes save themselves, so nothing is lost).
> - **A quieter bar on phones.** The bottom bar is now just Back, Forward and one search button. Tap it to find a note. Touch and hold it for Search inside notes, Look up a word, Today and More.

> [!info]- November 16, evening: Watch it, then play it
> - **Story Lines.** Week 1's story is now a short cartoon for each day, with Greek subtitles that light up as the characters speak. [Open it](https://www.perplexity.ai/computer/a/greekquent-story-lines-1bIJ0178Q2KldfTqtqgKZA), or tap **Watch it** under the day's line on Today.
> - **Text adventure.** The same scenes as an old-school text game: type the right Greek word to move the story on. Greeklish works, and HELP gives a clue.
> - More weeks are coming as the year's story is written.

> [!info]- November 16, overnight: A story every day
> - **Today's line.** Each day now has one short story line that uses that day's words (they are in bold). The same people all week: Μαρία, Νίκος, γιαγιά, παππούς, θεία and the νονός. Say it, tap Hear it, then tap **I said it**.
> - **The week in six lines.** Each line adds to the one before, so by Saturday you can tell a little story. On Sunday, Today shows the whole story to read aloud. Every week page has it too, under This week's story.
> - **Comebacks.** Lines you said 1, 3 and 7 days ago come back on Today. You see the English, say it in Greek, then tap to check. Spacing like this helps words stick ([a study of spaced practice with young learners](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/2331186X.2017.1287391)).
> - **Missed a few days?** Today picks up where you left off, one or two lines at a time, or you can jump to today. Nothing is lost.
> - **Kid track.** For younger learners: tap **Kid track** at the bottom of Today or in the More menu. Today then shows the kid lesson lines, one more each day, with the easy words (things you can point at) first ([research on easy-to-picture words](https://academic.oup.com/applij/article/43/2/293/6277142)).
> - **You are the teacher.** Every kid lesson now ends with a swap: the kid asks the questions and catches the grown-up's mistakes.
> - **New game: Γιαγιά.** Find 7 notebooks in the house before Γιαγιά feeds you. Each notebook is a word. [Open it](https://www.perplexity.ai/computer/a/greekquent-giagia-T2tsaLMvQiuN84Ng0un.IA), or tap Play Γιαγιά on Today.
> - **Cleaner examples.** Odd or grown-up example sentences on word cards and in the Anki deck were replaced with everyday ones.
> - **Updates run in the background.** When an update is ready, tap the notice and keep working. A small chip in the corner shows the progress. Your My Work is never touched.

> [!info]- November 16, late night: Three layouts
> - **A calmer start.** At the top of every page there is a small switch: **Simple**, **Intermediate**, **Advanced**. Everyone starts on Simple.
> - **Simple:** Today and this week's lesson stay bright. The rest of the file list is grayed out but still opens if you tap it. Tools: Look up, Send homework, My homework.
> - **Intermediate:** adds games, the word graph, your colors, past lessons, and your own word cards.
> - **Advanced:** everything, including Build a sentence, Pair it points, and Ask.
> - When you have marked enough words, Today suggests the next layout. Switch any time, in either direction. Nothing is deleted, and your choice is saved in My Work.

> [!info]- November 16, night: Smoother word graph
> - Tap a word in the word graph and its note now fades in gently instead of flashing in.
> - If your phone is set to reduce motion, it opens instantly as before.

> [!info]- November 16, evening: Your sentences on the word cards
> - Sentences you build with **Build a sentence** now show on the word note of every word they use, under Chunks, in **Yours**. That includes the ones you already saved.
> - Your own chunks and sentences show there too, each with a Hear button.
> - Nothing moved: they are still saved in My Work (My pairs and My word cards), so updates never erase them.

> [!info]- November 16, later: Your own chunks and Spider-Man
> - **Add to a word card:** on any word note, under Chunks, tap **Add a chunk or sentence**. Type the Greek, tap Translate for the English, hear it, and save. It shows on that word's note under **Yours**.
> - Everything you add is saved in My Work, in **My word cards**, so updates never erase it. Fix or delete lines there any time.
> - **Kid lesson 5 (Where is Spider-Man?):** new pass-it round. Έχεις τον Spider-Man; Ναι, έχω τον Spider-Man! Ορίστε. Ευχαριστώ!

> [!info]- November 16: Look up stays in Obsidian
> - **Bonus words are translated right here.** Type a word that is not in the 1,500 and the Greek shows up in the Look up box, with how to say it and a Hear it button. No more jumping to the browser.
> - **Words I looked up now saves the Greek** next to every bonus word.
> - Older look-ups that only had the English get their Greek filled in the next time you open Obsidian online. Anything you typed there yourself stays as it is.

> [!info]- November 14, late: Complete Greek
> - If you have the book Teach Yourself Complete Greek, each intermediate lesson now names the unit that goes with it. The audio is free in the Teach Yourself Library app.
> - Lessons 16 and 26 point to the book's revision tests.
> - No book? Nothing changes for you.

> [!info]- November 14, night: Textbook files
> - New note in Handouts: **00 Which file is which**. One page that says what every file is for.
> - The Fluent in a Year Anki deck (all 1,500 words) is now in Handouts.
> - The two textbook files in Handouts have the same lessons. Use Screen (color, lessons only) on your phone or tablet. Print (lessons plus Fluent in a Year) is the one to print, and it adds the Fluent in a Year planners.
> - The color cover is now the first page of both. The separate cover file is gone.

> [!info]- November 14, evening: Pair it
> - **Pair it with** on word notes: what to say with each word. Verbs show who, what, and how or when. Nouns show the verbs and describing words that go with them.
> - **Build a sentence:** tap one choice from each row and the app builds a correct Greek sentence. Hear it, then save it to My pairs.
> - **Your own pair** counts double. Try a partner we did not list.
> - **Today** shows your Pair it points for the week. Goal: 5 sentences.
> - **Word graph colors** now show the type of word: blue for verbs, purple for nouns, orange for describing words, teal for how, when and where.

> [!info]- November 14, later: clearer names
> - **Lesson pages:** "Student" is now **Beginner**, and "Kid variant" is now **Kid**. Your lesson pages are in Scripts/Beginner, and the kid lessons in Scripts/Kid.
> - **Setting up** now explains where the four tool buttons are on a computer and on a phone.

> [!info]- November 14: Today page and word colors
> - **Today** opens first: your 5 words for today, this week's lesson, and a short review list.
> - **Color your words** right on each word note: Don't have it, Kind of, Have it. Look up shows the color too.
> - **Play with your words:** the Today page opens the Buzzer or Cousins with today's words or your review words.
> - **Missed a word in Cousins?** Tap Save to my vault on the end screen. It shows up on Today for two weeks.
> - **Simpler toolbar:** Today, Look up, Ask, and More.
> - **Cleaner word notes:** the info line now says which lesson a word is first in.

## Lesson 1: What's in your bag

**Week of** Oct 26 · **This week:** έχω (I have)

**How to study this page:** cover the Greek, say it out loud from the English, then check. Saying it from memory works better than reading it again.

**Out in the world this week:** Pack a real bag with five things you can name in Greek. Tonight, take each one out and say Έχω ένα… out loud. Write a label by hand for one of them and stick it on.

### Today's phrases

Make the gesture every time you say the phrase. It helps the phrase stick.

| Phrase | Meaning | Gesture |
|---|---|---|
| **Γεια σας** | Hello (to a group, or polite) | Big wave to the whole room, fingers together and slightly bent. |
| **Γεια σου** | Hi (to one friend) | Small wave to one person, fingers together. |
| **Πώς σε λένε;** | What's your name? | Palm-up hand toward the partner, eyebrows up. |
| **Με λένε…** | My name is… | Hand flat on your own chest. |
| **Έχω ένα…** | I have a… | Hold the object up close to your body. |
| **Έχεις ένα…;** | Do you have a…? | Point at the partner's bag, eyebrows up. |
| **Ναι, έχω.** | Yes, I do. | Small Greek nod, head tipping down and to the side, and pat the object. |
| **Τι έχεις;** | What do you have? | Both palms up, shoulders slightly raised. |

#### Word list: 24 new words to black-mark

Find these on your printed word list (the number is the word's place on the list) and mark them in black today. At each review, re-mark them red, yellow, or green.

και (2) · εγώ (5) · σε (8) · ένας, μία, ένα (10) · εσύ (15) · σου (16) · έχω (17) · τι (18) · όχι (22) · ναι (23) · λέω (38) · σας (55) · ευχαριστώ (56) · πώς (66) · παρακαλώ (83) · γεια (96) · ορίστε (249) · το νερό (270) · το βιβλίο (394) · το κλειδί (632) · η τσάντα (645) · το κινητό (664) · το τετράδιο (1472) · το στυλό (1474)

### Main scene

**First day: what's in your bag?**: Two classmates meet before class and compare what they brought.

**New words:** σε, η τσάντα, και, ορίστε, ευχαριστώ, παρακαλώ

- A: **Γεια σου!** — Hi!
- B: **Γεια σου! Πώς σε λένε;** — Hi! What's your name?
- A: **Με λένε Μαρία. Εσένα;** — My name is Maria. And you?
- B: **Με λένε Νίκο.** — My name is Nikos.
- A: **Τι έχεις στην τσάντα;** — What do you have in your bag?
- B: **Έχω ένα βιβλίο και ένα στυλό. Εσύ;** — I have a book and a pen. You?
- A: **Έχω ένα κινητό, ένα κλειδί και νερό.** — I have a phone, a key, and water.
- B: **Έχεις ένα τετράδιο;** — Do you have a notebook?
- A: **Όχι. Έχεις ένα στυλό;** — No. Do you have a pen?
- B: **Ναι, έχω. Ορίστε!** — Yes, I do. Here you go!
- A: **Ευχαριστώ!** — Thank you!
- B: **Παρακαλώ.** — You're welcome.
- A: **Γεια σου, Νίκο!** — Bye, Nikos!
- B: **Γεια!** — Bye!

### Practice

#### Replays, swaps, and twists

Replay the scene with a partner, with the page face-down. Peek only when you get stuck. Change one thing each time.

**Swap one thing**

- Names: your own name · a Greek name card from a hat
- Objects: βιβλίο · στυλό · κινητό · κλειδί · τετράδιο · νερό
- Greeting: Γεια σου (one friend) · Γεια σας (a group, or polite)

**Twists to try with a partner**

- B answers Όχι to everything until the last item, so A has to keep asking.

**Every time**

- Trade parts with your partner.
- Ask about someone else (Έχει…; Θέλει…;).
- Retell round: tell the whole scene in Greek to three different partners, with less time each time (60, 45, then 30 seconds). When you're listening, just listen.

Cut out your Lesson 1 tiles (shaded tiles are verbs). Lay out the sentence mat, then for each sentence:

1. Build it from the English, then read it aloud.
2. Turn it into a question: swap the . for ; and raise your voice at the end.
3. Make it negative: put δεν right before the verb.
4. Swap one tile for another word from the extra tiles.
5. Write your last version by hand in your notebook.

- **A:** My name is Nikos.
- **B:** What do you have in your bag?
- **C:** Do you have a notebook?

## Lesson 2: Guest at a Greek home

**Week of** Nov 2 · **This week:** singular endings -ω/-εις/-ει

**How to study this page:** cover the Greek, say it out loud from the English, then check. Saying it from memory works better than reading it again.

**Out in the world this week:** Offer someone at home a drink in Greek (Θέλεις λίγο νερό;) and let them answer in English. Write the Greek letters you know on a sticky note by the kettle or coffee maker.

### Today's phrases

Make the gesture every time you say the phrase. It helps the phrase stick.

| Phrase | Meaning | Gesture |
|---|---|---|
| **Θέλεις λίγο νερό;** | Would you like a little water? | Offer an imaginary glass with both hands. |
| **Ναι, θέλω λίγο…, ευχαριστώ.** | Yes, I'd like a little…, thank you. | Pinch thumb and finger close together for "a little", then hand to heart. |
| **Όχι, ευχαριστώ.** | No, thank you. | Greek "no": tilt the head up with a small click of the tongue, then hand to heart. |
| **Θέλεις ένα γλυκό;** | Would you like a sweet? | Offer an imaginary spoon of spoon-sweet. |
| **Έχεις ψωμί;** | Do you have bread? | Mime tearing a piece of bread, eyebrows up. |
| **Ο Νίκος θέλει τσάι.** | Nikos wants tea. | Point at "Nikos", then mime holding a hot cup and blowing on it. |
| **…αλλά…** | …but… | One hand out, then the other hand out on the other side. |

#### Word list: 10 new words to black-mark

### Main scene

**Visiting the neighbor**: A guest arrives at a Greek neighbor's house. In Greece a host offers more than once, and a first "no" is expected.

**New words:** καλώς ήρθες, ο καφές, δεν

- Host: **Γεια σου! Καλώς ήρθες!** — Hi! Welcome!
- Guest: **Γεια σου, Μαρία! Ευχαριστώ.** — Hi, Maria! Thank you.
- Host: **Θέλεις λίγο νερό;** — Would you like a little water?
- Guest: **Ναι, θέλω λίγο νερό, ευχαριστώ.** — Yes, I'd like a little water, thank you.
- Host: **Θέλεις τσάι;** — Do you want tea?
- Guest: **Ναι, θέλω τσάι, ευχαριστώ.** — Yes, I'd like tea, thank you.
- Host: **Έχω και ένα γλυκό. Θέλεις;** — I also have a sweet. Would you like one?
- Guest: **Όχι, ευχαριστώ.** — No, thank you.
- Host: **Λίγο; Θέλεις λίγο;** — A little? Do you want a little?
- Guest: **Ναι, λίγο! Ευχαριστώ.** — Yes, a little! Thank you.
- Host: **Νίκο, θέλεις κι εσύ τσάι;** — Nikos, do you want tea too?
- Nikos: **Όχι, θέλω καφέ.** — No, I want coffee.
- Host: **Ο Νίκος θέλει καφέ, αλλά δεν έχω καφέ! Έχω τσάι.** — Nikos wants coffee, but I don't have coffee! I have tea.
- Nikos: **Ναι, τσάι!** — Yes, tea!
- Guest (to the class): **Η Μαρία έχει ένα γλυκό. Ο Νίκος θέλει καφέ, αλλά…** — Maria has a sweet. Nikos wants coffee, but…

## Lesson 3: Making plans

**Week of** Nov 9 · **This week:** -ώ stressed verb

**How to study this page:** cover the Greek, say it out loud from the English, then check. Saying it from memory works better than reading it again.

**Out in the world this week:** Make one real plan this week (coffee, a walk, a call) and ask for it in Greek first: Μπορείς αύριο; Write the plan on a paper calendar in Greek.

### Today's phrases

Make the gesture every time you say the phrase. It helps the phrase stick.

| Phrase | Meaning | Gesture |
|---|---|---|
| **Μπορώ;** | May I? | Reach toward an object and pause, eyebrows up. |
| **Ναι, βέβαια.** | Yes, of course. | Big open-handed "go ahead" sweep. |
| **Μπορείς;** | Can you? | Point at the partner and tap your wrist. |
| **Θέλω, αλλά δεν μπορώ.** | I want to, but I can't. | Reach out eagerly, then pull back and shake your head. |
| **Μπορείς σήμερα το βράδυ;** | Can you make it tonight? | Point down at the floor ("today"), then lay your head on your hands ("evening"). |
| **Λυπάμαι, δεν μπορώ.** | Sorry, I can't. | Hand on chest with a sad face, then a small head shake. |
| **Αύριο το πρωί μπορώ.** | Tomorrow morning I can. | Roll a hand forward ("tomorrow"), then stretch both arms up as if waking. |

## Lesson 4: Postcards and the cafe

**Week of** Nov 16 · **This week:** Τι…; + το/τον/τη

**How to study this page:** cover the Greek, say it out loud from the English, then check. Saying it from memory works better than reading it again.

### Today's phrases

Make the gesture every time you say the phrase. It helps the phrase stick.

| Phrase | Meaning | Gesture |

| **Τι βλέπεις;** | What do you see? | Point to your eyes, then to the partner, palms up. |

# Lesson 19: March 25th and directions

**How to study this page:** cover the Greek, say it out loud from the English, then check. Saying it from memory works better than reading it again.

>
> Example sentences, the scene task, and the Anki tags are on the week page: [[FY22 Directions|FY22 Directions]].

> [!question]- Group meet prompt · week 22
> **Directions**
>
> - **Πού είναι η τράπεζα;** (Where is the bank?)
> - **Πώς πάω στο κέντρο;** (How do I get to the centre?)
>
> **Bridge:** Give directions from where you are to a real place in town.
>
> **Use at least 5 of this week's words:** [[δεξιά]] · [[αριστερά]] · [[μπλε]] · [[πλατεία|η πλατεία]] · [[ευθεία]] · [[μακριά]] · [[απόλυτα]] · [[έλεγχος|ο έλεγχος]] · [[ανάγκη|η ανάγκη]] · [[επίθεση|η επίθεση]] · [[άδεια|η άδεια]] · [[επιχείρηση|η επιχείρηση]] · [[εντελώς]] · [[άρα]] · [[μωβ]] · [[καλώ]] · [[πουθενά]] · [[ανήκω]] · [[επάνω]] · [[γραμμή|η γραμμή]] · [[απόφαση|η απόφαση]] · [[αγώνας|ο αγώνας]] · [[συνάντηση|η συνάντηση]] · [[δήμος|ο δήμος]] · [[ολόκληρος]] · [[γεγονός|το γεγονός]] · [[κίνηση|η κίνηση]] · [[συμφωνώ]] · [[ξενοδοχείο|το ξενοδοχείο]] · [[ακολουθώ]]

**Out in the world this week:** Give someone directions in Greek from your front door to the kitchen, or to a store. Draw the route by hand and label each turn.

## Today's phrases

Make the gesture every time you say the phrase. It helps the phrase stick.

| Phrase | Meaning | Gesture |
|---|---|---|
| **Πού είναι…;** | Where is…? | Palms up, turning your head side to side. |
| **Μπορείτε να μου πείτε πού είναι…;** | Can you tell me where … is? | Polite hand on chest, then palms up, looking around. |
| **Πηγαίνετε ευθεία.** | Go straight ahead. | Chop a flat hand straight forward. |
| **δεξιά / αριστερά** | right / left | Point right, then left, with the whole arm. |
| **Είναι κοντά;** | Is it near? | Hold thumb and finger close together, eyebrows up. |
| **Είναι μακριά.** | It's far. | Throw an arm far out toward the horizon. |
| **Δεν βλέπω την πλατεία.** | I don't see the square. | Shade your eyes, look around, then shrug. |

## Review from earlier lessons

> [!question]- 8 review prompts
> Say each one in Greek out loud before you open the answers. Mark it red (didn't have it), yellow (sort of), or green (had it).
>
> 1. What's the weather like?
> 2. It's cold.
> 3. I'll watch a movie.
> 4. We'll go for a walk.
> 5. I want to learn Greek.
> 6. I speak a little Greek.
> 7. Can we go?
> 8. We're going to church. / Let's go to church.
>
> > [!success]- Answers
> > 1. **Τι καιρό κάνει;** (Lesson 18)
> > 2. **Κάνει κρύο.** (Lesson 18)
> > 3. **Θα δω μια ταινία.** (Lesson 17)
> > 4. **Θα πάμε βόλτα.** (Lesson 17)
> > 5. **Θέλω να μάθω ελληνικά.** (Lesson 15)
> > 6. **Μιλάω λίγα ελληνικά.** (Lesson 15)
> > 7. **Μπορούμε να πάμε;** (Lesson 11)
> > 8. **Πάμε στην εκκλησία.** (Lesson 11)

## Warm-up dialogue

> [!example]- Warm-up dialogue
> A: Συγγνώμη, μπορείτε να μου πείτε πού είναι η πλατεία;  
> B: Ναι. Πηγαίνετε ευθεία και μετά αριστερά.  
> A: Είναι μακριά;  
> B: Όχι, είναι κοντά. Βλέπετε την εκκλησία; Η πλατεία είναι εκεί.  
> A: Δεν βλέπω την εκκλησία…  
> B: Εκεί, δεξιά!  
> A: Α, ναι! Ευχαριστώ! Χρόνια πολλά!  

## Main scene

**Directions on the 25th of March**: A visitor asks for directions to the square on Independence Day.

**New words:** παρέλαση, 25η, μαρτίου, σημαίες

- A: **Συγγνώμη, μπορείτε να μου πείτε πού είναι η πλατεία;** — Excuse me, can you tell me where the square is?
- B: **Ναι, βέβαια. Πηγαίνετε ευθεία.** — Yes, of course. Go straight ahead.
- A: **Ευθεία…** — Straight…
- B: **Μετά δεξιά. Και μετά αριστερά.** — Then right. And then left.
- A: **Είναι κοντά;** — Is it close?
- B: **Ναι, είναι κοντά. Πέντε λεπτά.** — Yes, it's close. Five minutes.
- A (a few minutes later): **Συγγνώμη, δεν βλέπω την πλατεία. Είναι εδώ;** — Excuse me, I don't see the square. Is it here?
- C: **Όχι, η πλατεία είναι πίσω από την εκκλησία.** — No, the square is behind the church.
- A: **Ευχαριστώ!** — Thank you!
- C: **Πάτε για την παρέλαση;** — Are you going to the parade?
- A: **Ναι! Σήμερα είναι 25η Μαρτίου.** — Yes! Today is the 25th of March.
- C: **Χρόνια πολλά! Βλέπετε τις σημαίες; Η παρέλαση είναι εκεί.** — Happy holiday! Do you see the flags? The parade is over there.
- A: **Ναι, τις βλέπω! Ευχαριστώ πολύ!** — Yes, I see them! Thank you so much!

## Practice

> [!tip]- Replays, swaps, and twists
> Replay the scene with a partner, with the page face-down. Peek only when you get stuck. Change one thing each time.
>
> **Swap one thing**
>
> - Place: η πλατεία · η εκκλησία · το σχολείο · ο φούρνος · το φαρμακείο
> - Direction: ευθεία · δεξιά · αριστερά · πίσω από · δίπλα σε
> - Distance: Είναι κοντά. · Είναι μακριά. · Πέντε λεπτά.
> - An old line: work in one review phrase, for example **Τι καιρό κάνει;**
>
> **Twists to try with a partner**
>
> - Give wrong directions on purpose. The listener has to catch the mistake by retracing the route on a map.
>
> **Every time**
>
> - Trade parts with your partner.
> - Tell it about someone else (έχει, έχουμε, έχουν).
> - Tell it as tomorrow, with θα.
> - Retell round: tell the whole scene in Greek to three different partners, with less time each time (2 minutes, 90 seconds, then 1 minute). When you're listening, just listen.

> [!example]- Build it with tiles
> Cut out your Lesson 19 tiles (shaded tiles are verbs). Lay out the sentence mat, then for each sentence:
>
> 1. Build it from the English, then read it aloud.
> 2. Turn it into a question: swap the . for ; and raise your voice at the end.
> 3. Make it negative: put δεν right before the verb.
> 4. Swap one tile for another word from the extra tiles.
> 5. Write your last version by hand in your notebook.
>
> - **A:** No, the square is behind the church.
> - **B:** Are you going to the parade?
> - **C:** Είναι πίσω από την πλατεία.
>
> Extra tiles: δεν · ; · . · η πλατεία · η εκκλησία · το σχολείο · ο φούρνος

## This week at home

> [!note]- Homework and self-check
> **Homework (10 min a day)**
>
> - Read the main scene aloud once a day.
> - Draw and label a map of your neighborhood in Greek.
> - Practice the polite request with three places: Μπορείτε να μου πείτε πού είναι…;
> - Listen: open [Beginners' Greek audio](https://library.teachyourself.com/id007706138/Beginners-Greek-Audio) or the free Teach Yourself app, then choose **02.06 Conversation 1 · 02.08 Conversation 2 (replay Unit 2: where people come from and live, then give directions)**. Play each dialogue twice: once just listening, once saying it along with them.
> - Greek out there (these pages change every week): [Headlines: 25η Μαρτίου](https://news.google.com/search?q=25%CE%B7%20%CE%9C%CE%B1%CF%81%CF%84%CE%AF%CE%BF%CF%85&hl=el&gl=GR&ceid=GR:el) · [Watch](https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=Easy%20Greek%2025th%20of%20March) · [ERTflix](https://www.ertflix.gr/)
>
> **Can you do this without the page?** Give directions from the classroom to the front door or the kitchen.
>
> **By hand:** write your exit-ticket sentence on an index card and keep it. Red cards come back next week.
>
> **Anki (free):** say the answer out loud before you flip the card, and press Again until each card is right once that day.

**Capstone: three scenes**: Students perform three short scenes (café, plans, market), then celebrate the year.

**New words:** μπακλαβά

- Waiter: **Καλημέρα! Τι θέλετε;** — Good morning! What would you like?
- A: **Έναν καφέ και ένα νερό, παρακαλώ.** — A coffee and a water, please.
- Waiter: **Τίποτα άλλο;** — Anything else?
- A: **Έχετε γλυκό;** — Do you have anything sweet?
- Waiter: **Ναι, έχουμε μπακλαβά.** — Yes, we have baklava.
- A: **Ένα, παρακαλώ.** — One, please.
- B: **Τι θα κάνεις το Σαββατοκύριακο;** — What will you do this weekend?
- A: **Θα πάω στη θάλασσα. Θέλεις να έρθεις;** — I'll go to the beach. Do you want to come?
- B: **Θέλω, αλλά δεν μπορώ το Σάββατο. Έχω δουλειά. Την Κυριακή μπορώ.** — I'd like to, but I can't on Saturday. I have work. I can on Sunday.
- A: **Τέλεια, την Κυριακή στις δέκα!** — Perfect, Sunday at ten!
- A: **Πόσο κάνουν οι ελιές;** — How much are the olives?
- Seller: **Πέντε ευρώ το κιλό.** — Five euros a kilo.
- A: **Μισό κιλό, παρακαλώ.** — Half a kilo, please.
- Seller: **Ορίστε. Τίποτα άλλο;** — Here you go. Anything else?
- A: **Όχι, ευχαριστώ. Καλή σας μέρα!** — No, thank you. Have a good day!
- Teacher: **Μπράβο σε όλους! Καλό καλοκαίρι!** — Well done, everyone! Have a great summer!
- Everyone: **Καλό καλοκαίρι!** — Have a great summer!

## Practice

> [!tip]- Replays, swaps, and twists
> Replay the scene with a partner, with the page face-down. Peek only when you get stuck. Change one thing each time.
>
> **Swap one thing**
>
> - Café: καφέ · τσάι · νερό · γλυκό
> - Plans: θα πάω… · θα δω… · θα φάμε…
> - Market: ελιές · ντομάτες · ένα κιλό · μισό κιλό
> - An old line: work in one review phrase, for example **Χριστός Ανέστη! – Αληθώς Ανέστη!**
>
> **Every time**
>
> - Trade parts with your partner.
> - Tell it about someone else (έχει, έχουμε, έχουν).
> - Tell it as yesterday (ήθελα, πήγα…) or as tomorrow (θα…).
> - Retell round: tell the whole scene in Greek to three different partners, with less time each time (2 minutes, 90 seconds, then 1 minute). When you're listening, just listen.

> [!example]- Build it with tiles
> Cut out your Lesson 26 tiles (shaded tiles are verbs). Lay out the sentence mat, then for each sentence:
>
> 1. Build it from the English, then read it aloud.
> 2. Turn it into a question: swap the . for ; and raise your voice at the end.
> 3. Make it negative: put δεν right before the verb.
> 4. Swap one tile for another word from the extra tiles.
> 5. Write your last version by hand in your notebook.

> - **B:** What will you do this weekend?

>

Play each dialogue twice: once just listening, once saying it along with them.

# Lesson 5: Lost items and the shop

**Week of** Nov 30 · **This week:** δεν + verb; μου/σου

**How to study this page:** cover the Greek, say it out loud from the English, then check. Saying it from memory works better than reading it again.

> [!abstract]- Fluent in a Year · week 6 of 52 (optional tier): 30 words, 180 of 1,500 after this week
> Five new list words a day, Monday to Saturday. Sunday is review. Black-mark each word on your printed list the day you start it, then re-mark red, yellow, or green at review.

> **Fri · day 35:** [[μένω]] (I stay, I live) · [[γνωρίζω]] (I know, I meet) · [[χρησιμοποιώ]] (I use) · [[ελπίζω]] (I hope) · [[φέρνω]] (I bring)

>
> Example sentences, the scene task, and the Anki tags are on the week page: [[FY06 Lost and found|FY06 Lost and found]].

> [!question]- Group meet prompt · week 6
> **Lost and found**
>
> - **Πού είναι το κλειδί μου;** (Where is my key?)
> - **Δεν έχω το κινητό μου. Το έχεις εσύ;** (I don't have my phone. Do you have it?)
>
> **Bridge:** One person hides an object. The others ask with μου/σου until they find it.
>
> **Use at least 5 of this week's words:** [[πού]] · [[δύο]] · [[λεπτό|το λεπτό]] · [[πέντε]] · [[μισό]] · [[ευρώ|το ευρώ]] · [[πως]] · [[κάτι]] · [[κάποιος]] · [[έτσι]] · [[εσείς]] · [[όταν]] · [[μόνο]] · [[μας]] · [[μαζί]] · [[εκεί]] · [[σαν]] · [[ακόμα]] · [[του]] · [[αρχίζω]] · [[μένω]] · [[γνωρίζω]] · [[χρησιμοποιώ]] · [[ελπίζω]] · [[φέρνω]] · [[χαίρομαι]] · [[γυρίζω]] · [[φτάνω]] · [[πειράζει]] · [[δουλεύω]]

**Out in the world this week:** Find a Greek product in a grocery store (olive oil, feta, yogurt) and read one word from the label out loud. Copy that word by hand into your notebook.

## Rally

Class starts with this, all in Greek. The teacher asks, you answer, then you swap and ask. Practice your side before class: on Today, tap **Practice my side**. Stuck? Use [[11 Classroom Greek]].

- Teacher: **Γεια σας! Τι κάνεις;** — Hi, everyone. How are you?
- You: **Καλά, ευχαριστώ. Εσύ;** — Good, thanks. And you?
- Teacher: **Πού είναι το κινητό σου;** — Where is your phone?
- You: **Εδώ είναι!** or **Δεν ξέρω.** — Here it is! / I don't know.
- Teacher: **Έχεις τα κλειδιά σου;** — Do you have your keys?
- You: **Ναι, έχω τα κλειδιά μου.** or **Όχι, δεν έχω τα κλειδιά μου.** — Yes, I have my keys. / No, I don't have my keys.
- Teacher: **Μπορείς τώρα;** — Can you now?
- You: **Όχι, δεν μπορώ. Έχω δουλειά.** — No, I can't. I'm busy.
- Teacher: **Γιατί δεν μπορείς;** — Why can't you?
- You: **Γιατί δεν έχω ώρα.** — Because I don't have time.
- Teacher: **Πόσο κάνει;** — How much is it? (the teacher holds something up)
- You: **Δύο ευρώ.** or **Πέντε ευρώ.** — Two euros. / Five euros.

**Swap:** now you ask the teacher the same questions, then ask the person next to you.

## Today's phrases

Make the gesture every time you say the phrase. It helps the phrase stick.

| Phrase | Meaning | Gesture |
|---|---|---|
| **Δεν έχω…** | I don't have… | Turn out empty pockets or open empty hands. |
| **Πού είναι το κινητό μου;** | Where is my phone? | Pat your pockets, looking around. |
| **Δεν βλέπω…** | I can't see… / I don't see… | Hand over your eyes, head turning. |
| **Εδώ είναι!** | Here it is! | Point down hard at the spot and smile. |
| **Γιατί δεν μπορείς;** | Why can't you? | Both palms up, head tilted to the side. |
| **Έχω δουλειά.** | I have work. / I'm busy. | Mime typing fast. |
| **Μπορώ να δω;** | May I see? | Point at your eye, then at the object, eyebrows up. |
| **Πόσο κάνει;** | How much is it? | Rub thumb and fingers together. |
| **Δύο ευρώ.** | Two euros. | Tap two fingers on the counter, one coin at a time. |
| **Δεν ξέρω.** | I don't know. | Shrug with palms up. |

## Review from earlier lessons

> Say each one in Greek out loud before you open the answers. Mark it red (didn't have it), yellow (sort of), or green (had it).
>

> 2. What do you see?
> 3. Can you?
> 4. I want to, but I can't.
> 5. I have a…
> 6. Do you have a…?
>
> > [!success]- Answers

> > 2. **Τι βλέπεις;** (Lesson 4)
> > 3. **Μπορείς;** (Lesson 3)
> > 4. **Θέλω, αλλά δεν μπορώ.** (Lesson 3)
> > 5. **Έχω ένα…** (Lesson 1)
> > 6. **Έχεις ένα…;** (Lesson 1)

## Boards and reading

> [!info]- Lines to read aloud
> - Έχω νερό. → Δεν έχω νερό. Θέλω κρασί. → Δεν θέλω κρασί.
> - Θέλω, αλλά δεν μπορώ.
> - Το κινητό μου. Το κινητό σου. Η τσάντα μου. Τα κλειδιά σου.
> - Μπορώ να δω;

## Main scene

**Where's my phone? and the corner shop**: Part 1: a lost phone. Part 2: shopping at a small shop.

**New words:** μισό, το λεπτό, αυτός, πέντε, καλός, η μέρα

- A: **Ωχ! Πού είναι το κινητό μου;** — Oh no! Where's my phone?
- B: **Δεν ξέρω. Δεν βλέπω το κινητό σου.** — I don't know. I don't see your phone.
- A: **Δεν έχω το κινητό μου! Και τα κλειδιά μου;** — I don't have my phone! And my keys?
- B: **Τα κλειδιά σου είναι εδώ!** — Your keys are here!
- A: **Ευχαριστώ! Αλλά το κινητό μου;** — Thanks! But my phone?
- B: **Είναι στην τσάντα σου;** — Is it in your bag?
- A: **Όχι, δεν είναι… Μισό λεπτό… Εδώ είναι!** — No, it isn't… Wait a second… Here it is!
- B: **Τέλεια! Μπορείς τώρα; Θέλω καφέ.** — Great! Can you come now? I want a coffee.
- A: **Όχι, δεν μπορώ. Έχω δουλειά.** — No, I can't. I'm busy with work.
- B: **Γιατί δεν μπορείς;** — Why can't you?
- A: **Γιατί δεν έχω ώρα!** — Because I don't have time!
- A: **Καλημέρα! Μπορώ να δω;** — Good morning! May I look?
- Seller: **Ναι, βέβαια.** — Yes, of course.
- A: **Πόσο κάνει;** — How much is it?
- Seller: **Δύο ευρώ.** — Two euros.
- A: **Και αυτό;** — And this one?
- Seller: **Πέντε ευρώ.** — Five euros.
- A: **Δεν θέλω αυτό. Θέλω το βιβλίο. Ορίστε δύο ευρώ.** — I don't want this one. I want the book. Here are two euros.
- Seller: **Ευχαριστώ! Καλή μέρα!** — Thank you! Have a good day!

## Practice

> [!tip]- Replays, swaps, and twists
> Replay the scene with a partner, with the page face-down. Peek only when you get stuck. Change one thing each time.
>
> **Swap one thing**
>
> - Lost item: το κινητό μου · τα κλειδιά μου · η τσάντα μου · το βιβλίο μου
> - Where: εδώ · στην τσάντα · στο τραπέζι · κάτω από το τραπέζι
> - Price: ένα ευρώ · δύο ευρώ · πέντε ευρώ
> - An old line: work in one review phrase, for example **Βλέπω τη θάλασσα.**
>
> **Twists to try with a partner**
>
> - The shopkeeper says Δεν έχω… to everything, and the customer has to keep asking for something else.
>
> **Every time**
>
> - Trade parts with your partner.
> - Ask about someone else (Έχει…; Θέλει…;).
> - Retell round: tell the whole scene in Greek to three different partners, with less time each time (60, 45, then 30 seconds). When you're listening, just listen.

> [!example]- Build it with tiles
> Cut out your Lesson 5 tiles (shaded tiles are verbs). Lay out the sentence mat, then for each sentence:
>
> 1. Build it from the English, then read it aloud.
> 2. Turn it into a question: swap the . for ; and raise your voice at the end.
> 3. Make it negative: put δεν right before the verb.
> 4. Swap one tile for another word from the extra tiles.
> 5. Write your last version by hand in your notebook.
>
> - **A:** Your keys are here!
> - **B:** Is it in your bag?
> - **C:** Why can't you?
>
> Extra tiles: δεν · ; · . · το κινητό μου · τα κλειδιά μου · η τσάντα μου · το βιβλίο μου

> - Spot today's letters on Greek signs, menus, or labels online.
